chapterTitle: Forward Interest Rates, FRAs, and Term Structure Theories

scenes.title: The Future Borrowing Dilemma
scenes.concept: Raju needs a ₹5 Crore loan 1 year from now; Sharma ji introduces forward rates and FRAs to lock the rate today.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju worries interest rates will spike before his plant expansion next year
beatOutlines.speaker: Raju

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji explains that current zero rates already define forward interest rates
beatOutlines.speaker: Sharma ji

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju asks how an OTC contract can fix his borrowing cost today
beatOutlines.speaker: Raju

scenes.title: Expectations vs Liquidity Preference
scenes.concept: Contrast pure rate expectations with investor liquidity preference driving yield curve slopes.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Expectations Theory asserts forward rates equal expected future spot rates
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Liquidity Preference Theory proves investors demand a premium for locking cash long-term
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Forward rates systematically exceed expected future spot rates by a liquidity buffer
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Continuous Forward Rate Formula
scenes.concept: Derive R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1) with 3% 1-year and 4% 2-year worked example.

beatOutlines.textOutline: The implied forward rate bridges zero rate growth across consecutive horizons
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Continuous formula: R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1)
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If 1-year is 3% and 2-year is 4%, year 2 forward rate is exactly 5.0%
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Synthetic Forward Rate Replication
scenes.concept: Show no-arbitrage proof: borrowing for T1 and investing for T2 synthetically locks forward borrowing.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Strategy A: Borrow for period T1 at rate R1 to fund cash needs today
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Strategy B: Invest for period T2 at rate R2 to receive cash flow at T2
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Net cash flow at T0 is zero; forward rate R_F is locked with zero basis risk
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Forward Rate Agreement (FRA) Architecture
scenes.concept: Explain FRA terms, fixed payer vs floating payer, and corporate interest rate risk hedging.

beatOutlines.textOutline: FRA is an OTC contract setting fixed interest rate R_K for future period T1 to T2
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Fixed Rate Payer receives floating rate R_M, hedging against rising interest rates
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Floating Rate Payer receives fixed rate R_K, protecting lenders against falling rates
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Principal is purely notional; only the net interest difference is exchanged
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: FRA Cash Settlement at Time T1
scenes.concept: Master the discounted advance settlement formula at time T1.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Standard loan interest is paid at maturity T2: Payoff = L*(R_M - R_K)*(T2 - T1)
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Advance settlement occurs at time T1, requiring discounting by [1 + R_M*(T2 - T1)]
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Discounted settlement ensures economic equivalence without counterparty risk during loan term
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Valuation of an FRA Prior to Maturity
scenes.concept: Compare initial zero-value contract with marked-to-market valuation as forward rates evolve.

beatOutlines.textOutline: At inception: contract rate R_K is set equal to market forward rate R_F, so V_FRA = 0
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Mid-life valuation: V_FRA = L*(R_F - R_K)*(T2 - T1)*e^(-R2*T2)
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Changes in forward rates create immediate balance sheet gains or losses
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: Orange County Bankruptcy: Repo Leverage Trap
scenes.concept: Analyze Snapshot 4.1: $13B short repo leverage, inverse floaters, and $1.6B loss.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Bob Citron geared $7.5B county equity into a $20.5B portfolio using $13B short repo
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Invested in medium-term inverse floaters that paid high yields when rates fell
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In 1994, the Fed raised rates 6 times by 250 bps; repo borrowing costs surpassed bond yields
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Orange County suffered $1.6B losses, collateral liquidations, and municipal bankruptcy
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

scenes.title: The Whole Picture: 8 Core Term Structure Rules
scenes.concept: Execute strict 8-step summary sequence covering all chapter principles with dedicated Rule 8 focus.

beatOutlines.textOutline: Executive overview of all eight forward rate and term structure principles
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 1 & 2: Forward rate formula and no-arbitrage synthetic borrowing replication
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 3 & 4: FRA hedging mechanics and discounted advance settlement at time T1
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 5 & 6: Pre-maturity FRA mark-to-market valuation and Liquidity Preference Theory
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Rules 7 & 8: Orange County repo leverage disaster and 2008 interbank liquidity freeze
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Final 2-column whole-chapter reference matrix
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: 1. Forward Rate Formula: Continuous forward rate R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1) is implied by zero rates.
2. No-Arbitrage Replication: Borrowing for T1 and investing for T2 synthetically replicates forward loans.
3. FRA Hedging Architecture: Fixed payers receive floating R_M and pay fixed R_K to cap borrowing costs.
4. Advance Settlement Discount: FRAs settling at time T_1 divide payoff by [1 + R_M*(T_2 - T_1)].
5. Pre-Maturity Valuation: Existing FRAs are valued by discounting the spread between R_F and R_K.
6. Liquidity Preference Reality: Forward rates exceed expected spot rates (R_F > E[R]) by a positive liquidity buffer.
7. Orange County Lesson: Funding long assets with $13B short repo leverage destroyed $1.6B during Fed rate hikes.
8. Interbank Liquidity Freeze: Crisis spreads blew out to 364 bps when commercial paper markets froze.
bottomTakeaway: Forward rates represent no-arbitrage break-evens; liquidity preference creates normal upward slope, and FRAs lock future borrowing costs.
